Introduction

A Health Care Service Firm (HCSF) in New Jersey provides non-medical home care services including personal care, homemaker, and companion services. The NJ Department of Health — Division of Certificate of Need & Licensing oversees HCSF licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand New Jersey’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand New Jersey’s Regulations

The NJ DOH licenses HCSFs under N.J.A.C. 8:45. Requirements include licensing, background checks via the Criminal History Record Information Act, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

HCSFs provide personal care, homemaker, companion, and chore services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the NJ Division of Revenue, apply for HCSF license, secure insurance, and obtain a Certificate of Need if required.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

New Jersey benchmarks: Private pay rates $24-$35/hour, Medicaid rates $18-$26/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, technology systems, and quality tools.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

NJ requires background checks and competency training for all staff.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting NJ DOH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks across NJ’s diverse communities and healthcare systems.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and ongoing compliance.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is an HCSF? A Health Care Service Firm provides non-medical home care staffing and services.
